Enormous monolith, carved 9350 years ago, found under Mediterranean Sea

I'd love to hear an archaeologist's take on this. From the article's pictures I wasn't 100% convinced that this man made but I am a complete layman on this topic. If it is genuine, does this change our understanding of human society during this time period?

It's almost certainly man-made and this doesn't really change our understanding of what people were doing back then by a whole lot in itself, but it does provide further evidence of a pattern of megalithic monument construction that was significantly earlier than we previously thought. This monolith was made right at the very beginning of megalithic architecture, and it was built while the area was still above sea level. An even older and more sensational site that's mentioned in the article, Gobekli Tepe, is located about 1,100 miles away.

Before Gobekli Tepe (and - assuming some consensus is reached on its age and veracity - this site), the assumption was that hunter-gatherers settled down, began practicing agriculture, and then started building monuments a few generations or even a few thousand years later. These extremely early examples of monumental architecture have raised the possibility that the monuments came first and people started to become less nomadic and practice agriculture later, which is backwards from the traditional understanding of that development. It's also raised the possibility of things being a lot more chaotic in terms of technological advancement at that point, with some areas gaining monumental architecture and then agriculture, and other areas gaining agriculture and then monumental architecture. This megalith is 1000-2000 years younger than Gobekli, but both of them coincide roughly with the period of the neolithic revolution, which is the transition between hunter-gatherer and agrarian subsistence practices.

Good answer. The idea that hunter-gatherers, or early farmers were "primitive" is very dated now. Shame the article repeats them. I'd like to know how they can be so accurate in their dating.... 9350 BP is very exact.
